name: Clean Room White
lede: Clean Room White is a pale yellowish white matched to the industrial standard RAL 9012, about 3 units from ivory.

sections.title: An industrial white
sections.body:
This white is filed against RAL 9012 in the German RAL registry, founded in 1927 for coatings and signage [1]. The ISCC-NBS system classes the hue as a yellowish white [2]. "Clean room" names the dust-controlled manufacturing spaces this white is associated with, rather than a dye, pigment or place, and no source consulted gives an exact coining date [1].

In our library the nearest named color is [[ivory]], about 3 units away by CIEDE2000, with [[cream]] close behind on the warmer side [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: ColorHub's archive finds this near-white in 69 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [4]. It peaks in paintings from Nepal, Iran, Korea and China, and in the 1850s decade specifically [4]. A pale wash like this is as likely to come from aged varnish or a lit sky as from any single pigment [4]. The match is computed, not a pigment identification [4].
